Build a feature's per-group statistics table from raw MS1+MS2 data.table

Source: R/spectral_filtering.R
process_pseudo_spec.Rd

Turns one feature's raw rows into a per-group statistics table:

Usage

process_pseudo_spec(
  dt,
  mz_target,
  grouper = ppm_upgma(ppm = 30),
  group_statistics_fn = correlation_statistics(),
  buffer = 50L,
  consensus_mz_fn = NULL,
  apex_source = c("recompute", "upstream"),
  window_mode = c("buffer", "fwhm")
)

Arguments

dt

One feature's rows from batch_get_feature_data().

mz_target

Precursor m/z, passed to the grouper as target_mz.

grouper

A grouper closure (grouper-contract).

group_statistics_fn

A statistics closure (stats-contract).

buffer

With window_mode = "buffer", keep scans with abs(ms1_scan - apex) < buffer.

consensus_mz_fn

A consensus-mz closure (consensus-mz-contract); NULL uses consensus_mz_weighted().

apex_source

"recompute": the scan with the highest MS1 intensity in dt. "upstream": dt$apex_scan; samples where it is NA are dropped with a warning.

window_mode

"buffer": fixed scan window (see buffer). "fwhm": walk out from the apex until MS1 intensity drops below half the apex intensity, within the scans present in dt.

Value

The statistics table; zero rows if nothing is left at any step.

Details

  1. Drop rows without a fragment.

  2. Find each sample's apex scan (apex_source) and keep the scans around it (window_mode).

  3. Group the fragment m/z of all samples together with grouper.

  4. Compute one consensus m/z per group (consensus_mz_fn).

  5. Score the groups with group_statistics_fn.

No filtering is applied; clean_pseudo_spectra() adds that.
